question: Now that FY2026 (Apr 2025-Mar 2026) has closed, has the audited standalone/consolidated Annual Report been published, and do the audited full-year figures materially differ from the Q4 FY2026 investor-presentation figures used throughout this analysis (revenue 17,843 cr, PAT 5,816 cr, EBITDA 8,613 cr, all consolidated, company-summarised)?
why_it_matters: F-FUND-01, F-FUND-02, and F-FUND-10 all rely on FY2026 full-year figures sourced only from the Q4 PPT (AR FY2026 unpublished per orchestrator brief); RF-MERGE-14/15/16 already document a precedent divergence between AR-sourced and PPT-sourced FY2025 figures (PAT 5,267.94 cr AR vs 5,325 cr PPT) of similar magnitude to what could recur for FY2026. This blocks full confidence on the FY2026 growth-deceleration and margin-normalization findings until confirmed against audited figures.

question: What is the standalone (not just consolidated) FY2026 P&L and balance sheet, and does the standalone-vs-consolidated near-identity established for FY2020-FY2025 (F-FUND-09) continue to hold for FY2026?
why_it_matters: The primary-basis conclusion (standalone as the appropriate basis for valuation/estimates) rests on five years of near-identical standalone/consolidated figures; FY2026 is the one year in this dataset available only on a consolidated (PPT) basis. If JV/subsidiary contribution has grown materially in FY2026 (e.g., if Utkarsha or Angul Aluminium Park activity picked up), the standalone-primary convention should be revisited once the FY2026 AR is available.

question: Once the 0.5 MT smelter project reaches DPR/tender stage (targeted Aug-Sept 2026 per RF-GUI-03) and a firm capex schedule and funding mix (debt vs internal accruals vs GoI equity infusion) is disclosed, what is the projected incremental ROCE and payback profile for the Rs.18,000 cr program?
why_it_matters: F-FUND-03 establishes that NALCO's largest-ever capex program has not yet started (still pre-DPR) and that no incremental-ROCE analysis is currently possible; this is a mandatory analysis item (capex & returns engine) per the module's required-analyses list and remains the single largest unresolved capital-allocation question for the thesis. Blocks estimates-builder's ability to model post-FY2027 ROCE/ROE trajectory with any precision.

question: Is any portion of the 0.5 MT smelter capex (Rs.18,000 cr) or the coal-block/refinery capex program planned to be debt-funded, and if so what is management's target leverage/D-E ratio for the build phase (FY2027-FY2031)?
why_it_matters: F-FUND-07 identifies a tripling of standalone finance costs (off a near-zero base) as a possible leading indicator of a shift away from NALCO's historical all-equity-funded capex model; simultaneously, F-FUND-... (capital allocation tension) notes dividend per share rose 2.6x in FY2025 (10.5 vs 4.0) even as the largest capex program in company history is beginning. Without a stated funding mix, forward interest-cost, leverage, and dividend-sustainability estimates cannot be built with confidence.

question: What specifically drove the ~Rs.400 cr (24%) FY2026 capex overshoot versus the Rs.1,700 cr original budget -- cost inflation on the 5th-stream refinery, schedule compression, scope additions, or a different project entirely?
why_it_matters: F-FUND-04 flags the overshoot as disclosed but unexplained in the current fact set; a recurring pattern of capex overshoots would compound the guidance-reliability concerns already logged in RF-GUI-01/RF-GUI-03 (schedule slippage) into a broader capex-guidance-quality read (both cost and schedule guidance proving unreliable in year one of the largest capex program in company history).

question: What is the composition of NALCO's FY2025/FY2026 current borrowings (124.22 cr FY2025 consolidated) -- is this working-capital/bill-discounting financing tied to the capex ramp, buyer's credit for imported inputs (caustic soda, coal), or something else -- and is any of it expected to convert to longer-tenor debt as the smelter capex begins?
why_it_matters: F-FUND-07 flags the ~243% YoY rise in standalone finance costs (17.2 cr to 59.0 cr) as directionally worth monitoring but currently immaterial; understanding the borrowing composition would clarify whether this is transient working-capital noise or the earliest signal of the capital-structure shift relevant to OQ-FUND-04.

question: What are sell-side/consensus estimates (if any exist externally) assuming for FY2027 alumina and aluminium (LME) price decks, and how do they compare to management's own FY2027 guidance (alumina US$300-310/t, metal US$3,000-3,100/t per QT-Q4-052/QT-Q4-083)?
why_it_matters: F-FUND-10 shows Q4 FY2026 already running at negative YoY revenue/PAT, and F-FUND-01/F-FUND-02 establish that FY2025's margin peak is cyclical and already reversing. Estimates-builder needs an external anchor (consensus or peer commodity-price decks) to sanity-check whether management's FY2027 price guidance is conservative, in-line, or aggressive relative to market expectations -- this is inherently an external-research question, not answerable from company documents alone.

question: Why did Chemicals (alumina) segment EBIT grow proportionally faster than Aluminium (metal) segment EBIT in FY2025 (Chemicals EBIT share of the combined pool rose from 38.8% in FY2024 to 44.5% in FY2025, per F-DER-FUN-07/08) even though the revenue mix moved the other way (toward metal, 70% to 73%) over the same period?
why_it_matters: F-FUND-08's claim that the metal-mix shift is straightforwardly margin-supportive is only partly borne out by the segment EBIT data; reconciling this (e.g., alumina segment's own internal transfer-pricing treatment, or a base-effect from FY2024's depressed alumina EBIT) is needed before the segment-mix narrative can be used cleanly in the valuation/sensitivity work without an internal contradiction.
